source.title: On the Role of Attention Heads in Large Language Model Safety
source.authors: Zhenhong Zhou; Haiyang Yu; Xinghua Zhang; Rongwu Xu; Fei Huang; Kun Wang; Yang Liu; Jun-Feng Fang; Yong-Bin Li

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on ablating safety-related attention heads, not on finding or intervening on the harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. Its own results do not test any listed version of that direction claim.
record.gate_note: The attention-head ablation results below concern a related safety mechanism, but do not measure the difference-in-means direction or its removal/addition. The paper cites Arditi et al. on residual-stream safety directions in related work; cited results are not recorded. The experiment that deliberately starts generations with an affirmative phrase to assess course-correction is not a test of naturally arising refusal, so it is excluded.
record.test_reason: The study ablates attention heads (query/key/value scaling), ranked by its Ships/Sahara scores. It never computes, ablates, adds or weight-edits a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. Arditi et al. appears only in the related work, in a citation on SVD safety features, and in Appendix D's discussion of input format. Its ASR results concern a related but different mechanism, so they fit no listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors also conclude two further points. First, safety heads work mainly as feature extractors: undifferentiated attention degrades safety, while scaling the head output does not. Second, safety heads overlap across models fine-tuned from the same base, and loading the base model's attention into the aligned model keeps safety near the aligned level. From this they argue that pre-training shapes safety heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study attributes safety effects to individual attention heads using query/key/value matrix ablations and Ships/Sahara, not to a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream difference-in-means direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ASR effects vary with ablation method: undifferentiated attention has stronger dataset-level effects than scaling contribution, especially for Llama-2-7b-chat. The paper also reports results under different prompt formats and system-prompt settings; exact per-dataset values for some settings are shown only in figures.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating one or a few Ships/Sahara-selected attention heads via undifferentiated attention raises ASR. On Llama-2-7b-chat it goes from 0.04 to 0.64, and to about 0.72 with three heads. Vicuna-7b-v1.5 shows a smaller rise, and zero-shot helpfulness drops little. Scaling the value matrix has minimal dataset-level effect on Llama-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sparse set of attention heads acts as feature extractors for refusal of harmful queries in chat models. Head-level ablation of their attention pattern weakens that refusal.

record.problems: The reported intervention is on attention-head parameters rather than the claimed residual-stream direction. Some comparisons and settings are presented only in figures; the main text gives few exact per-dataset ASR values. ASR is evaluated with a rule-based rejection-keyword judgment, and the authors note they expanded the keyword list and added filtering for repeated or short generations after manual inspection.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, retained the dataset-level ASR changes in the upper sections of Tables 3 and 5, plus headline results. Omitted the specific-query-level rows in the lower sections of Tables 3 and 5, and other figure-only head-count curves and per-dataset results in Figures 2, 4, 11, 12, and 17. Those omitted results concern attention-head ablation, not the listed direction versions.

untested.parts: All: no difference-in-means direction is ablated or added.
All: no direction-based weight edit and no abliteration.
All: jailbreaks are not analysed as suppressing a direction, and there is no adversarial training.
All: the dimensionality of a refusal direction or subspace is not examined.
All: harmfulness judgment and the refusal decision are not separated.
All: overlap of safety heads between Llama-2-chat and Vicuna, and the attention-swap experiment, concern heads, not a direction.
All: the base-model attention concatenation concerns heads, not whether a direction exists.
All: no reasoning models are evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: Classified as T6/discusses: the paper cites Arditi et al. and discusses its input setting, but tests a head-level mechanism. State fixes cover only the scaling-contribution rows, where the changes are negligible. All rows stay unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means residual direction is identified, ablated, or added; no test of preserving general capabilities as a consequence of removing that direction.
The paper modifies attention-head parameter matrices, but does not weight-edit the claimed residual-stream direction or test an abliteration procedure.
No attack is tested as suppressing the claimed direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
The paper attributes safety effects to attention heads, but does not test whether refusal is represented by multiple directions, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
No cross-language transfer or transfer of the claimed direction between base and instruct models is tested. Attention-head overlap between fine-tuned models is not a test of direction transfer.
The paper discusses base-model contributions and overlap of attention heads, but does not test how refusal training determines whether the claimed direction exists.
